purpose: Document which internationally respected art-school practices are retained and how they are converted into practical working-artist outcomes.

integrations.khaemenes_use: ARTS-111; immediate portfolio evidence; observation/visual decision-making; no prestige gatekeeping.
ARTS-121; composition, color, photography, digital imaging and commercial/presentation relevance.
ARTS-131; object, installation, scale, construction and material problem-solving.
ARTS-131 and ARTS-211; sound, sequence, motion, performance, video and cross-media experimentation.
ARTS-141; museums, galleries, archives, living artists, visual culture and research notebook feeding studio decisions.
Weekly Tuesday critique and formal critique units; revision must produce observable changes or documented decisions.
Artist statements, bio, proposals, applications, research context and source integrity tied directly to the learner's own work.
At least one collaborative/community experiment in ARTS-211.
ARTS-131 practical material safety, waste, reuse and responsible production decisions.
ARTS-221, ARTS-251 and ARTS-298 require audience testing, exhibition/public presentation and professional documentation.
Year 1 explores broadly; Year 2 selects signature practice, niche and cohesive body of work.

rejected_or_reframed: Mandatory expensive materials when accessible alternatives teach the same skill
Critique that rewards jargon over revision
Portfolio polish without pricing, marketing, client or sales literacy
Theory isolated from the student's own studio practice
A single Western canon presented as the default definition of art
